name: What is the biggest mistake people make when designing a home addition?

mainEntity.name: What design mistake most often causes additions to feel awkward or expensive later?
mainEntity.text: What design mistake most often causes additions to feel awkward or expensive later?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common mistake is treating the addition like a stand-alone room instead of part of a complete house. Homeowners often focus on square footage first and discover later that setbacks, structure, roof transitions, circulation, and daylight create major problems. An addition that looks good on a sketch can become difficult to build or disappointing to live in if it blocks light, creates awkward hallways, or overwhelms the original home. Another frequent mistake is ignoring how the new space will connect to the existing plan. The best additions improve the way the whole house functions, not just the new area. That means studying the site, understanding the structure, and testing several layouts before committing to one. When those issues are handled early, the result is usually more efficient, more attractive, and easier to permit and build.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest mistake is starting with room size instead of site constraints, structure, and circulation. When the design does not account for setbacks, roof tie-ins, light, and how people move through the home, the addition can become expensive to build and awkward to live in. Good design solves the whole house, not just the new room.
